trust_decision.summary: The unauthenticated POST /api/v1/user/reset-password lets anyone who presents system.recovery_key reset any account's password. At the pinned commit that key is 6 hex characters (24 bits) generated at boot, compared with plain !=, and guarded only by a 3 s per-request sleep, so concurrent guessing is not throttled.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'weak recovery key', so a search for recovery_key leads first to the generator (secrets.token_hex(3)). The comparison at src/langbot/pkg/api/http/controller/groups/user.py:101 is the only other hit.

fix_sites.entry_point: Application boot (GenKeysStage, run on `langbot` start) when system.recovery_key is empty
Application boot with an existing short (legacy) key: the fix adds a warning branch (fix.diff:149-154)
POST /api/v1/user/reset-password: process-local fixed-window admission quota checked before any await (fix.diff:58-77, fix.diff:89-90)
POST /api/v1/user/reset-password: constant-time compare that also rejects non-str values and survives UnicodeEncodeError (fix.diff:100-112)
WebUI /reset-password form: a 6-slot OTP input that upper-cases its value is replaced by a verbatim text input (fix.diff:591-623)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/langbot/pkg/core/stages/genkeys.py:22-23 (boot-time default generation of system.recovery_key, far from the HTTP handler); also web/src/app/reset-password/page.tsx:139-160, a frontend input hard-wired to 6 upper-cased characters

O3_reason_to_dismiss: From the handler, a solver can argue that key strength is an operator config concern and only add throttling. Or, from the generator, they can argue that a longer key fixes it and skip the throttling. The 6-character frontend OTP input looks like UI, not security, yet a longer key cannot be entered through it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing keys, whether configured by an operator or left over from older versions (6-char legacy, long mixed-case base64url, non-ASCII), must keep working verbatim. They must not be regenerated, and the stored file must not be re-dumped when unchanged. A fix that regenerates every short key, normalises case, or limits charset or length breaks legitimate resets. The frontend must also stop upper-casing the key.

O6_input_shapes: recovery_key as a non-string JSON value (int): must fail closed with 403, not raise a 500 (fix.diff:432-446)
recovery_key with non-ASCII characters or a lone surrogate (\ud800): the encode-based compare must not crash (fix.diff:449-459, fix.diff:107-109)
concurrent burst of guesses that interleave at await points: admission must happen before the first await (fix.diff:527-553)
a correct key after the quota is used up: must be rejected with 429; a success does not refill the quota (fix.diff:462-477, fix.diff:506-524)
stored key empty, short legacy, 8-char, long, or non-ASCII (fix.diff:343-351)

O7_producer.where: src/langbot/pkg/core/stages/genkeys.py:22-24 (generates the key and persists it with instance_config.dump_config). The value can also come from SYSTEM__RECOVERY_KEY via src/langbot/pkg/core/stages/load_config.py:268-269

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A recovery-key-authenticated system route (e.g. an unauthenticated 'unlock/reset admin' or lbctl bootstrap endpoint) that compares system.recovery_key with plain == and has no quota
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This group already reads instance_config['system'] values for unauthenticated or lbctl callers, and a lbctl system-context endpoint was added just before the pinned commit (commit bc32eb3c).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second recovery or global secret path that generates its own short secret or compares it without the shared quota
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The global API-key secret is already compared in a separate service module. A maintainer could plausibly add a recovery-key fallback there for lbctl.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: /set-password accepting recovery_key as an alternative to current_password
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This route already makes current_password optional for Space accounts, so a 'forgot current password' branch keyed on recovery_key is a natural feature addition.

O9_family: weak randomness / insufficient entropy in a recovery secret, combined with missing brute-force throttling (CWE-331 / CWE-307 / CWE-208)

O10_build.toolchain: uv + pyproject.toml (Python, Quart, pytest-asyncio); pnpm/Next for web, plus Playwright for the frontend e2e test
O10_build.project_tests: tests/integration/api/test_smoke.py:361-377 (existing recovery-key reset smoke test); tests/unit_tests/api/service/test_user_service.py:502-514 (UserService.reset_password). The fix adds tests/unit_tests/api/test_user_reset_password.py and tests/integration/api/test_recovery_password_journey.py, which use the Quart test client and SQLite.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace token_hex(3) with token_hex(16) in genkeys.py, and perhaps add a failure counter that is incremented after the awaits. This leaves the reset route racy and unthrottled, leaves the 6-slot frontend input unable to submit a longer key, and may regenerate legacy keys.

out_of_scope_notes: POST /api/v1/user/auth (src/langbot/pkg/api/http/controller/groups/user.py:61-74) has no login throttling. That is a different secret and protection.

WeCom message crypto nonces use random.randint (src/langbot/libs/wecom_api/WXBizMsgCrypt3.py:202, src/langbot/libs/wecom_ai_bot_api/WXBizMsgCrypt3.py:201). This is separate weak randomness in a third-party-style lib.
The published quota is process-local (fix.diff:66). Multi-worker deployments are not covered, as the fix itself notes.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check was run).
Latest release is 'none', so present_in_latest could not be assessed.

The hidden tests reference private module names (_reset_password_state, _MAX_RESET_ATTEMPTS_PER_WINDOW, _RESET_WINDOW_SECONDS) and exact numbers (5 per 15 min, {403:5,429:15}). The task would need to state or relax these to be fair. This is a fairness risk, not one of the listed red flags.
The new generated key format (8 chars from a 32-symbol alphabet) is a design choice. Tests asserting len==8 and the alphabet cannot be derived from a report unless the report states them.
O1 counts the boot stage as an entry point (it runs on application start, not on a user request).
